what: Markup attribution accuracy across the corpus — ROADMAP measure 3, which the roadmap records as 'currently unmeasured'. This is the first measurement.
how: Every annotation in a *.json expectation carries `intendedTargetId`: the component a person would say the markup refers to. `correct` counts the annotations whose actual binding equals it.
misses: annotated/note-2 — binds to the CVC input; a person would say the totals card.
notes: The test asserts `correct` never falls below this number, and fails if `total` changes — a corpus that grew needs the baseline re-reviewed by hand, not bumped.

2026-11-16 (SPEC-005): the corpus grew by one, frame-screens' note 'Move this to a header bar', typed in a real tab 33px under S02's 'Sign out' inside a frame. It binds to s02-out, where a person would say it belongs: 5/6. The five older annotations bind as before.

2026-11-17 (SPEC-006): the corpus grew by two, markup-legend's marks drawn in a real tab: a red note 19px left of the Password field (and 13px from the legend, which the reading leaves out), and a green ring round Sign in. Both bind where a person would say: 7/8. annotated's marks were recoloured, which moved no binding.

2026-11-17 (PR 1, round 1): the corpus grew by one, the first mark a person drew: a green loop round all of S01 of the owner's dnd_crawler_rust wireframe, which the person confirmed means 'S01 is fine'. It bound to a heading inside the screen, a miss: 7/9. The same day KI-10's fix let a ring round a whole container target it, and the loop binds to the screen: 8/9. The round had one mark in all, so it is no measurement of the loop by itself (KI-3 stays open).

9 annotations is a small sample: eight drawn by an agent imitating a person, one by a person (human-round-1). The real measurement is ROADMAP PR 1, where a person marks a canvas up and N is whatever they drew; its first round, 2026-11-17, gave N = 1. Treat this as a regression guard, not as evidence the loop works.
